Special Manoeuvres

Special manoeuvres may be necessary from time to time. These include:

🚗
Driving Away
Pulling away after waiting or parking on the side of the road, e.g. from a parking space.
⬅️
Reversing
Moving the vehicle backwards.
🏗️
Entrance / Exit Construction
Recognised by a continuous pavement with lowered kerbs or exit blocks. Drivers leaving preferably have right of way.
↩️
(U-)Turning
Turning the vehicle to drive in the opposite direction.
🛣️
Getting in Lane
Entering the main carriageway from the acceleration lane.
🚪
Exiting
Entering the deceleration lane from the main carriageway.
↔️
Changing Lanes
A sideways manoeuvre where you move from one lane to the adjacent lane.

Giving Way

When performing a special manoeuvre, you must give way to all other traffic. For example, when entering an entrance construction, you must not hinder pedestrians — whether they are on the pavement or on the carriageway at the time.

This also applies when driving away, reversing, (U-)turning, getting in lane, exiting, and changing lanes.

Sometimes you have to deviate from your line (an important lateral movement) — for example to go around something or through a road narrowing. In that case, you must give way to oncoming traffic. If both drivers need to deviate, they may mutually decide who goes first. In many cases, signs regulate this.

F-5
Oncoming traffic (including pedestrians) may go first. This sign only applies to drivers approaching it.
F-6
Oncoming drivers must let you go first — even if you are a pedestrian.
⚠ Heavy Vehicles & the Verge

On a narrow road, someone may have to go into the verge. Note that heavy vehicles such as lorries and passenger cars with trailers cannot enter the verge — they risk sinking or falling over. In that case, the other driver must make extra space.

💡 With combined insertion and exit lanes (weaving lanes), it is best that the exiting driver takes precedence over the inserting driver, as the exiting driver often has more speed.

Indicating

Indicating is mandatory so other traffic knows what you are planning. You must indicate when:

🔆 Mandatory Indicating Situations
  • Driving away
  • Overtaking other motor vehicles
  • Getting in lane
  • Exiting
  • Changing lanes
  • Making important lateral movements
Important lateral movement

Moving so far to the left or right that it is safer to indicate such to other traffic in advance.

Indicating when overtaking a cyclist or moped rider is not mandatory in itself — because these are not motor vehicles. However, if you have to make an important lateral movement to do so, indicating is mandatory nonetheless.

⚠ Indicating is intended to make clear what you are going to do. Do not use it to force others to give way to you!

Important Points to Note

When performing a special manoeuvre, keep in mind:

  • The manoeuvre must be as short as possible.
  • The manoeuvre must cause as little hindrance as possible to other traffic.
  • Road safety must not be endangered.
  • The manoeuvre must be permitted at the location where you perform it.
📍 Where are special manoeuvres prohibited?

Special manoeuvres are only allowed in places where this is permitted. You may not turn, stop, or reverse on the motorway or autoweg. Reversing and turning in a one-way street is also prohibited. U-turning may additionally be banned by sign F-7.

C-3
One-way street — U-turning and reversing are not allowed here
F-7
U-turning ban

Bus Leaving a Bus Stop

Drivers normally give way to all other traffic when driving away. There is one important exception:

🚌 Bus Stop Exception

Drivers must give way to bus drivers indicating an intention to leave a bus stop — but only within built-up areas.

This applies to all buses, but only when using the indicator. Outside built-up areas, this does not apply.

Passengers Getting On or Off the Bus or Tram

At some tram or bus stops, passengers board and alight in the middle of the road. Check whether there is a traffic island (refuge) or central reservation for waiting passengers.

🧍 No refuge / island present

You must give way to passengers crossing the road.

🏝️ Refuge / central reservation present

Giving way is not mandatory — passengers can wait there safely.

🚶 Getting In & Out of Your Own Car

When you get in or out of the car yourself, you are a pedestrian and must give way to drivers.

When entering: walk towards the door against traffic (e.g. if parked on the right, walk in front of the car). Only approach the door when you can immediately get in quickly.

When getting out: open the door only after checking no one is coming. Walk back to the pavement against traffic.
